module_title: Major Industries - Basic Classification and Key Industries
introduction: Manufacturing is the process of converting raw materials into more valuable products. The economic strength of a country is heavily measured by the development of its manufacturing industries. In geography, industries are primarily classified based on the source of their raw materials: Agro-based and Mineral-based. At this beginner level, we will understand the foundation of India's largest and most crucial industries.

core_concepts.title: Agro-Based Industries
core_concepts.description: These industries obtain their raw materials directly from agricultural products. Major examples in India include Cotton Textiles, Jute, Silk, Woolen textiles, and the Sugar industry. The Cotton Textile industry is the largest, oldest, and most widely spread industry in India, providing employment to millions of weavers and farmers.

core_concepts.title: Mineral-Based Industries
core_concepts.description: These industries use rocks and minerals as their primary raw materials. The 'Iron and Steel Industry' is the most massive example. Other significant industries in this category include Aluminum smelting, Cement, and various Chemical industries.

core_concepts.title: Iron and Steel: The 'Basic' Industry
core_concepts.description: The Iron and Steel industry is called a 'Basic Industry' because all other industries (whether heavy, medium, or light) depend on it for their machinery, tools, and infrastructure. Because its raw materials (iron ore, coking coal, and limestone) are extremely heavy and bulky, these steel plants are always established close to the mining areas to minimize transport costs.

core_concepts.title: Cotton Textile Clusters
core_concepts.description: Historically, the cotton textile industry was highly concentrated in the black cotton soil regions of Maharashtra and Gujarat. 'Mumbai' and 'Ahmedabad' emerged as the largest and most traditional centers. This was due to the immediate availability of raw cotton, excellent port facilities for export, a humid climate (which prevents the yarn from breaking), and cheap labor.

important_entities.name: TISCO (Jamshedpur)
important_entities.key_fact: India's First Modern Iron and Steel Plant
important_entities.significance: The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 at 'Sakchi' (now Jamshedpur) in Jharkhand, situated at the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers. It was a completely private sector plant and laid the foundation for India's modern industrial revolution.

important_entities.name: First Successful Cotton Mill
important_entities.significance: While handloom cotton textiles had been produced in India for centuries, the very first successful 'mechanized' cotton textile mill was established in Mumbai in the year 1854, marking the beginning of the modern factory system in India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Manchester in the UK was globally famous for its cotton textiles. In India, exams often try to trick you with regional titles. Remember: 1. Manchester of India (or the West) = Ahmedabad (Gujarat). 2. Manchester of North India = Kanpur (UP). 3. Manchester of South India = Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu). Always read the directional keyword in the question.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To produce steel in a blast furnace, the ideal ratio of the bulky raw materials required is approximately 4 parts Iron Ore, 2 parts Coking Coal, and 1 part Limestone.

exam_strategy_tips: If an exam asks which industry is the second-largest provider of employment in India after agriculture, the correct answer is always the 'Textile Industry'.
Whenever you see the term 'Basic Industry' or 'Key Industry' in a multiple-choice question, immediately select 'Iron and Steel'.
